summary: Lease entropy split causes cohort duplication and cascading fallbacks during canary prewarm
description: Issue summary: During a staged canary prewarm for a model rollout (canary v.2026-03-09), some tenant cohorts were duplicated across edge shards due to non-deterministic lease entries. This produced mixed routing (requests hitting two different model variants for the same session) and triggered fallback routing rules, causing intermittent degraded variants to serve traffic and a short spike in per-token costs and 5xxs for affected tenants. Impact: Multiple dedicated customers (notably Novalearn) observed mixed model outputs and elevated error rates. The behavior persisted for ~45 minutes before initial mitigation. This ticket tracks support coordination, SRE investigation, mitigation steps, and follow-up actions.
impact: Customer-visible mixed responses (generation text from two variants) and transient 5xxs. Billing spike observed for affected tenants due to fallback to higher-cost degraded variants and repeated prewarm attempts. Primary customer Novalearn reported interrupted demo flow and increased latency. Approximately 12 tenant cohorts impacted in us-east and eu-west, estimated extra cost ~ $2.3k during the window.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Trigger a staged canary prewarm that uses prewarm-mirroring + orchestrator snapshot merge (replicate prewarm on warm pool).
2) Simulate small clock skew between two orchestrator replicas and prewarm mirror enabled.
3) Initiate tenant traffic for a long-lived streaming session pinned to the canary cohort.
4) Observe that the same session ID surfaces leases on two different edge shards with different model_variant fields.
5) Requests start routing inconsistently, and the fallback policy engages when one variant returns throttling/latency violations.

investigation_notes: Timeline: 14:02Z duplicate lease creation observed shortly after canary prewarm start. Service-level alerts triggered at 14:06Z when fallback rules fired due to latency/5xx counts on canary nodes.

Evidence: Orchestrator logs show two lease_create entries (different lease_id hex values) for the same tenant/cohort within 200ms on different replicas. The orchestrator snapshot merge process writes leases without a strong de-duplication key when prewarm-mirror is enabled.

Hypothesis: During prewarm mirroring we create a mirrored lease record on a warm pool which raced with the authoritative lease writer on the primary orchestrator replica. Because lease ids were generated locally (not deterministically), the merge produced two valid-looking leases. Edge proxy reconciler treats the first-seen lease as authoritative for routing; when the second lease appears on a different shard the session can be routed inconsistently depending on shard-level cache TTLs.

Secondary effect: kvcache tombstone entries from previous prewarms were not fully reconciled during the merge leading to tombstone_collision errors and stale pin retention in some shards. This caused fallback policy (which equates unresponsive variant with degraded variant) to trigger more aggressively.

Metric evidence: p95 latency for canary nodes rose from 180ms to 1.2s for affected shards; 5xx rate increased from 0.08% to 1.7% for Novalearn's traffic window. Billing logs show extra prewarm attempts + fallback variant traffic producing ~ $2.3k extra cost in the window.

Cross-references: Slack thread #support-incident-lease-entropy and runbook page for lease reconciliation contain relevant context. Related PRs opened to address non-idempotent lease generation and to add a snapshot-merge acceptance test.

Scope: Initial triage indicates ~12 tenant cohorts impacted across us-east and a small subset in eu-west where mirrored prewarm was active and orchestrator replicas had slight clock skew (~150ms) during the merge.

Reproduction status: Reproduced in staging using a Canary prewarm job with two orchestrator replicas and simulated non-deterministic lease generator. Confirmed duplicate lease creation and routing divergence in the edge-proxy tests.

Root cause (preliminary): Non-deterministic lease_id generation + snapshot-merge logic that didn't dedupe leases by (tenant, cohort) led to duplicate authoritative lease records across shards. TTL and tombstone handling in kvcache amplified the routing divergence and fallback activation.
resolution_notes: Mitigation applied 2026-03-10 14:28Z: Paused prewarm-mirroring for canary in us-east; ran lease revocation script that removes secondary lease_id records and forces orchestrator to reconcile authoritative lease set. Result: Novalearn confirms demo recovered at 14:58Z.

Short-term fix deployed 2026-03-11 02:18Z: Config change ensures lease_id generation is now derived from deterministic tuple (tenant, cohort, epoch) for prewarm mirror operations to avoid collisions during merges. Deployed behind a feature flag. PR: https://github.com/redwood/reconcile/pull/2140.

Long-term fix planned: Update snapshot-merge codepath to perform deterministic deduplication by (tenant, cohort) with last-write-wins semantics and add post-merge kvcache reconciliation step to clear tombstones safely. Add unit and integration tests that simulate orchestrator replica clock skew and prewarm mirror merges. ETA for full rollout: 2026-03-24.

Operational follow-ups: 1) Add alert 'duplicate_lease_detected' with automated mitigation (pause mirroring + revoke duplicate) and tie to runbook. 2) Add canary rollout checklist item: 'verify deterministic lease generation when prewarm-mirroring enabled'. 3) Schedule postmortem with Novalearn and internal stakeholders (SRE, Orchestrator, Edge) for 2026-03-16.

Customer communication: Sent interim update to Novalearn 2026-03-10 16:10Z confirming mitigation and ongoing engineering work. Follow-up committed to include timeline for permanent fix and offer billing credit for excess costs. Finance & CS to coordinate credit approval.

Lessons learned: Prewarm-mirroring introduces additional state merge complexity; deterministic IDs and idempotent reconciliation are required for safe snapshot merges. KV cache tombstone handling must be hardened to avoid amplified divergence during merges.
